Acme Integrator: Hey team — onboarding hit a weird snag. SDK handshake works from local but fails from our staging behind corp proxy. Getting intermittent 401 then bursts of 429s. Not sure if token scope or proxy is mangling TLS. Anyone seen this pattern?

Emma (CS): Sorry you're hitting that. Can you paste the client logs around the first 401? Also which SDK and version?

Acme Integrator: Using node-sdk v0.9.2. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-09T14:02:12Z] POST /v1/chat 401 {"error":"invalid_client"}
[2026-03-09T14:02:12Z] retrying token refresh
[2026-03-09T14:02:14Z] POST /v1/chat 429 {"error":"rate_limited","retry_in":2}
[2026-03-09T14:02:16Z] POST /v1/chat 429
```
We proxy via corp-gw (TLS intercept). No cert errors in app, but root cert installed on hosts.

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Two separate things to consider: (1) 401 then 429 often means the client retried quickly with same key but proxy replays/queues requests causing bursts. (2) TLS intercept can rewrite SNI or alter connection pooling, which messes upstream auth headers if the proxy re-signs TLS or does connection splitting.

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Quick checks: set REDWOOD_API_KEY explicitly on the staging container, confirm no token rotation script is running. Run a single deterministic request (curl) that forces no retries then inspect headers:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --noproxy "*" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
If curl works from the host but the app fails, it's likely SDK-level retry/backoff + proxy behaviour.

Emma (CS): Also try forcing the SDK to use a single connection / disable keepalive to see if connection pooling is triggering the rate bursts. In node-sdk you can set env var REDWOOD_SDK_NO_POOL=1 for diagnostic.

Acme Integrator: Good tip. I'll toggle that. Also we use an internal sidecar that adds a header X-Client-Proxy: corp-gw. Could that be causing something?

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Possibly. Our side will treat unknown forwarded headers normally, but if the proxy does request splitting (e.g., terminates TLS and opens multiple backend connections) and the SDK immediately retries on 401 with exponential backoff but starting small, you can get a cluster of retry requests landing within the time window and trip the per-key rate limiter.

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Workarounds: (a) increase the SDK initial backoff so retries are spaced out: set REDWOOD_RETRY_BASE_MS=250 and REDWOOD_RETRY_MAX_MS=8000 for staging; (b) enable jitter: REDWOOD_RETRY_JITTER=1; (c) use token caching if you rotate tokens frequently.

Emma (CS): From an onboarding perspective, I can temporarily bump rate limits for your org so you don't hit 429s while we diagnose. Would you like me to open a short-term lift (30m) to confirm fixes? :thumbsup:

Acme Integrator: Yes please — that'd help isolate path. If lift is on and we still see 401 then it's auth rotation issue.

DeployBot: [automated] Created temporary quota lift for org acme-corp: +200 req/min for 30 minutes (ID: lift_2026_179600).

Acme Integrator: Thanks Emma. After bump we still saw occasional 401s but far fewer 429s. I turned off the sidecar and set REDWOOD_SDK_NO_POOL=1 — that removed the bursty 429s. Still investigating 401s.

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Great repro. For 401s check dt: are you using short-lived service tokens that rotate in the background? If so, ensure the SDK refresh is atomic — you can use our recommended pattern: single refresh mutex per process. If apps fork workers, ensure only the parent refreshes the token and children inherit it.

Acme Integrator: We do rotate tokens via a vault agent. It refreshes the file on disk and our process reads it. Could there be a race so some requests attempt with an old token while rotation is in progress?

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Yes — that leads to transient 401 then immediate retry => 429. Two options: have the vault agent write to a temp file then atomically mv to token path; or add short-lived acceptance window on our side by enabling a small grace period for rotated tokens (we can enable grace for your org for testing).

Emma (CS): I'll coordinate with infra to enable token-grace for acme-corp for 2 hours so you can roll properly. Also we'll keep the quota lift until you confirm.

Acme Integrator: Appreciate it. Next steps for us: switch vault agent to atomic write, re-enable sidecar, set REDWOOD_RETRY_JITTER=1 and REDWOOD_SDK_NO_POOL=0, and test. We'll report back in ~30m.

Ajay (Solutions Eng): Also FYI if you must run behind TLS interceptors long-term, consider a bypass for calls to api.redwood.* or use a corporate allowlist. When that's not possible, test with increased initial backoff and jitter.

Emma (CS): Noted — I'll follow up with a short doc summarizing these steps and a recommended diag checklist.

Acme Integrator: Update: after atomic writes + jitter we are stable. No 401s or 429s in 45m of soak. Thanks all. :party:
